properties.label: Thermal conductivity
properties.conditions: air-laid nonwovens with 30 to 70% milkweed at about 11 to 19 kg/m3, -4 to 24 C

timeline.event: A US wartime milkweed pod collection enlisted schoolchildren to gather pods for life vest filling under the slogan 'Two bags save one life'.
Oil sorption of milkweed, kapok and polypropylene fiber assemblies was compared.
A field experiment found that up to 90% of monarch eggs on common milkweed in grasslands were lost within 72 hours.
Milkweed floss was characterized as a natural hollow, oleophilic sorbent.
Air-laid nonwovens made with Quebec-grown milkweed reached thermal conductivities of about 28 to 35 mW/m K for building insulation.

properties.label: Intrinsic Young's modulus
properties.conditions: estimated by micromechanics and corrected single-filament tests

timeline.event: Henequen leaf juice, a decortication by-product, was hydrolyzed and fermented to ethanol.
Micromechanical modeling put the intrinsic Young's modulus of henequen fiber at roughly 30 to 35 GPa.
A thin cell layer protocol for somatic embryogenesis was published to multiply elite Agave fourcroydes clones.
Henequen leaves were studied as a source of textile fiber, with thermal stability up to about 220 C.

properties.conditions: both fleece types, Peruvian llamas, by that study's classification

timeline.event: The US Wool Products Labeling Act named llama among the specialty fibers that may be labeled as wool.
Genetic analysis placed the llama with the guanaco lineage, clarifying a long-disputed ancestry.
A smart system for assessing medullation and diameter of alpaca, llama and mohair fibers was developed and validated.

timeline.event: North American bison, which had numbered in the many millions, were reduced to near extinction.
Crossbreeding with cattle was promoted, leaving cattle ancestry in many modern bison herds.
A conservation genetics review concluded that modern plains bison descend from fewer than 100 founders.
A survey of mitochondrial DNA across 14 plains bison herds in the US and Canada was published.

properties.conditions: common brushtail possum fur, New Zealand

timeline.event: The first releases of brushtail possums in New Zealand failed to establish.
A possum population was established in Southland.
Some 36 batches of possums were imported, and by 1930 releases had been made at about 450 locations.
All protection was removed and the possum came to be treated as an environmental pest.
A study found that fur harvest for economic return and possum control for biodiversity can pull in different directions.

timeline.event: J. A. Freeman gave the first medical description of mercurialism in hatters, in the Transactions of the Medical Society of New Jersey.
Mercury use in US hat felting was curbed when mercury was needed for wartime detonators.
Regulation (EU) No 1007/2011 reserved the name angora for Angora rabbit hair, separating it from generic rabbit hair on EU labels.

timeline.event: John Boyd Textiles began weaving horsehair fabric in Castle Cary, England.
Mechanical looms that pick one hair at a time were developed for horsehair weaving.
Regulation (EU) No 1007/2011 listed horsehair among the Annex I textile fiber names.
